cohort: Pregnant females aged 16-44 years with Sickle Cell Disease and Medicaid insurance, along with a control cohort of pregnant people, identified from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Service Analytic eXtract.
finding: Pregnancy-related complications and maternal death were significantly more common in people with Sickle Cell Disease compared to controls, and these adverse outcomes did not improve, and some even increased in frequency, between 2006 and 2018.
